content.text: Support has three tickets from this morning saying people got the Monday roundup email two and in one case three times over. Work out what happened and stop it.

content.content: claimed_at is NULL for 1,412 of 1,412 rows in send_batch

content.thinking: If claimed_at is null for every row then nothing ever took ownership of the batch, so a second worker would happily start from the top of the same list.

content.text: The weekly digest is enqueued once by the 07:00 cron, but the sender was scaled to two replicas last Thursday and neither replica claims the batch before it starts sending. Both replicas walked the same list, so every recipient on the Monday list was reached twice. Nothing downstream deduplicates: there is no per-recipient send key, so a second delivery to the same recipient looks exactly like a first one.

Claiming is now a conditional UPDATE that sets claimed_at only where it is still null, and the sender skips any batch it did not claim. Re-ran the replay against the Monday list: 1,412 sends, no repeats.
